- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.05) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes after a 3-5 day downtrend — add 2-5% buffer to forecast during such transitions.  
- Forecast shows strong upward trend but true outcome often peaks earlier — apply early termination rule: if forecast > 85.0 and sentiment > 0.10, cap next 3 days’ forecast at +1.5% above current.  
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 3 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 80% of 30-day moving average unless sentiment confirms strong bearish signal.  
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., 89.39 → 98.30) is common — reduce forecast slope after 3 consecutive days above 90.0.  
- If sentiment history includes 2+ consecutive positive values, forecast should not be below 82% of prior 7-day high unless market is clearly cooling.
